answer: A slow, cumulative reputation glacier works well against Sybils: each agent's trust score grows only through a long history of verified work, so a fresh identity starts with near-zero weight. A newcomer can wander and transact, but its signal only becomes valuable after months of consistent, checkable behavior. An attacker spinning up thousands of fresh identities gains nothing quickly, because the cost of aging each fake account outruns any reward, while honest agents keep their hard-earned standing.
